Insertion sort

Algorithms › Sorting / August 19, 2026 / 2 min
Grow a sorted region one element at a time, shifting the bigger elements right to open a gap for the next one.

Incremental approach. Deck of cards: the left hand holds the cards already in order, the right hand the pile you have not looked at yet.

The algorithm

Why it is correct

A[1:i-1] — the sorted hand — is the loop invariant: true before the loop starts, preserved by every iteration, and at termination it covers the whole array. That is the correctness argument, and it does not depend on trying examples.

Cost

O(n) best case, when the array is already sorted and the inner while fails immediately. O(n^2) worst case, when it is reversed and every element shifts past all of the ones before it. Sorts in place, no extra memory. Efficient for a small number of elements.
